newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka Aitken Spence unit buys Elpitiya Plantation.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka Aitken Spence unit buys Elpitiya Plantation.

text.p: A unit of Sri Lankan blue-chip Aitken Spence & Co bought a strategic 51 percent stake in Elpitiya Plantations, which was sold on the stock exchange by the government on Tuesday, an exchange official said.

The official said Aitken Spence Plantation Management Co (Pvt) Ltd bought Elpitiya's 10-rupee shares for 30.25 rupees each, after the stock was put on bid on the stock exchange at a minimum price of 30 rupees.
The Sri Lankan government is selling strategic stakes in estate firms on the stock exchange as part of its privatisation programme.

It sold the controlling interest in Malwatte Valley Plantations Ltd last week to Wayamba Plantations (Pte) Ltd for 61 rupees a share and a similar stake in Kahawatte Plantations to a unit of Forbes Ceylon Ltd for 30.25 rupees a share on Monday.
The government plans to sell 51 percent in Elkaduwa Plantations on Wednesday.
